title: What If the Sun Suddenly Went Out?

scenes.text: What if the Sun went out right now? For eight minutes, you wouldn't even know.
Sunlight and gravity both take about eight minutes to arrive, so Earth keeps orbiting and glowing until then.
Then darkness. Photosynthesis stops at once, and the average surface temperature falls below zero Fahrenheit within about a week.
After one year it's around minus 100 degrees. Most plants die within weeks, though big trees can last decades.
The oceans freeze from the top, but that ice insulates the deep water, which could stay liquid for hundreds of thousands of years.
Life wouldn't vanish. Microbes in Earth's crust and vent creatures run on the planet's own heat, not sunlight.

description:
What if the Sun suddenly went out?
